rationale: The candidate reads as one continuous but generic inflated bar with modest plan irregularity; it is coherent in all four views, so it avoids view-specific collapse, but the mass remains too sealed and typologically bland for the neighborhood-living brief. The thick blue frontage edge is not answered by a clearly public ground threshold: there is no obvious notch, court, undercut, or entry seam aligned to the access side. The top and oblique views suggest a slight carve, yet it does not register as a usable public void. Silhouette continuity is acceptable, but the section is not yet doing enough work for an active street edge or a mixed-use ground program. Compared with the references, it has less courtyard/public-space legibility and less sectional generosity. The strongest corrective direction is to preserve the dominant inflated anchor while carving a clearer access-side void or notch to create public ground and program-relevant hierarchy.
